note: Expected results for the frozen core at the time this fixture was written. 'supported' records whether the three-source triangle is expressible today; 'gap' names what is missing. Assertions live in tests/unit/finance/test_reconciliation_triangle.py.

s2_fee_invoice_vs_naive_bank.gap: A bank row has no fee column, so a 29.00 fee difference lands in the gross component and is classified as a refund lag. Fee-aware matching needs the processor's gross/fee bound to the deposit.

s3_many_to_one.gap: reconcile() has exactly one processor leg and one ledger leg. No type, allocator, or entry point accepts N charges against one deposit, so a payout cannot be expressed at all.

s4b_partial_payment.gap: A 400.00 shortfall with no refund is classified as a refund/capture lag. There is no partial-payment code, so underpayment is indistinguishable from refund timing.

s5b_missing_deposit.gap: reconcile() requires a ledger leg. A charge with no bank line produces nothing, so 'missing' and 'not yet arrived' share the same non-result.

s6_duplicate_bank_row.gap: The duplicate flag cannot fire once nets agree (exact_match wins), so dedup must run before reconcile; find_duplicates/ensure_unique do catch the pair.

s7_ambiguous_allocation.gap: 970.00 could come from three charges or one; find_match() returns the first equal-net candidate and reports no ambiguity, so a wrong-but-plausible allocation is silently accepted.
